title: v1/chat.completions: harmonize role mapping & stop semantics; stabilize streaming envelopes
author: Elena Martinez
description: Motivation: customers using the /v1/chat.completions compatibility layer reported subtle regressions when combining role aliases, multi-entry stop arrays, and long-lived streaming sockets; additionally some downstream SDKs expect logprobs and function_call envelopes in a stable, minimal format. This PR harmonizes role->internal persona mapping, normalizes stop token inputs to a canonical array-of-strings form, and introduces an envelope-versioning field for stream chunks to make client-side framers resilient to mixed encodings. Changes are backward-compatible by default: we accept legacy stop formats and role aliases, emit a compatibility header in streaming chunks for older SDKs, and add an opt-in compatibility flag (`openai_mode=legacy`) to preserve previous exact byte-level framing for customers that need it. The PR bundles runtime fixes, SDK input sanitizers, and a targeted test matrix. Checklist: 1) role mapping table + normalization implemented; 2) stop param normalizer (string/array/nested-array) + dedupe; 3) streaming envelope versioning + small heartbeat/ack fields; 4) logprobs output normalized to the openai v1 shape when requested; 5) tests added for C++/Go runtimes and Python/TS SDKs; 6) docs/compatibility notes updated. Context/notes: this is a production-sensitive change; feature gated on a compatibility flag and default behavior preserves client-visible semantics except for cases where previous behavior was ambiguous (e.g., nested stop arrays).
